Live, winning outcome tokens are ERC-1155 CTF positions that must be redeemed (redeemPositions on the CTF / negRisk adapter, or claimed via Polymarket's relayer/proxy wallet) before the USDC is spendable again, and self-redeeming from an EOA needs POL for gas. Nothing in the repo redeems, claims, or mentions this; venue_facts.md:27 notes venue settlement lands only ~20-60s after window end.
findings.evidence: paper.py:126-127: "payoff = pos[\"shares\"] * (1.0 if won else 0.0); pnl += payoff - pos[\"cost\"]" -- cash conjured at internal settle time. Grep for redeem/claim/gas/matic across bot/ returns nothing but doc comments (src/costs.py:7 "Winning shares redeem $1").
findings.failure_scenario: 5m markets settle every 5 minutes; at full caps a coin can lock $150-600 per cycle. If redemption is not automatic on this account's setup, buying power monotonically drains: with a $1,500 wallet and ~$300/coin-cycle across 5 coins, spendable USDC hits zero within the first hour while the paper-style P&L view says everything is fine -- every subsequent order dies at the hold's balance re-validation, and the edge (which lives on being present in the final 30-60s) silently stops harvesting.
findings.fix: Build stage 5: determine on the FIRST dry-run trade whether the operator's account setup (Polymarket proxy wallet vs raw EOA) auto-credits winnings; if not, add a redemption worker sweeping resolved condition ids every 1-2 minutes (batch redeemPositions; hold 5-10 POL -- redemptions cost cents on Polygon). Size day-1 bankroll at >= 10x configured concurrent exposure so a redemption stall degrades throughput, not correctness, and alert when spendable balance < 2x per-order cost.

findings.title: Position state is self-belief with no venue reconciliation, even on restart
findings.claim: broker.positions is built exclusively from the bot's own simulated fills, and the restart path (_replay_open_positions, run.py:113-162) replays the bot's OWN paper_fills.jsonl -- correct for paper, but live it re-derives belief from belief. There is no comparison against the venue's positions/balance (Polymarket data-api), no divergence alarm, and the per-market caps, the opposite-side guard (run.py:979-985) and the daily loss limit all run on this unverified ledger.
findings.evidence: run.py:113-114: "def _replay_open_positions(self): \"\"\"Rebuild positions in STILL-OPEN markets from the fills log.\"\"\"" -- the only position-recovery mechanism; no code anywhere queries a venue position or balance endpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: A live fill whose ack was lost (crash between POST and ack persistence) is absent from the log; after restart the bot sees zero shares in a market where it holds 100, buys the full cap again (the documented 2x-cap failure this function exists to prevent, resurrected by the paper-to-live gap), or buys the OPPOSITE side the guard would have blocked -- paying ~$1.90 for a $1.00 payoff, an instant ~47% loss on the doubled stake.
findings.fix: Build stage 5: on startup and every 60s, fetch positions and balance for the wallet from the data-api, diff against the local ledger, and on any mismatch: halt new orders for that market (or all, if balance diverges), log a reconcile_mismatch line, fire the alert webhook. Persist sent-order intents (order id, size, market) to disk BEFORE the POST so the restart path queries each unresolved order id instead of trusting the fill log.

findings.title: Kill switch gaps: no stop-all script, and the daily kill un-arms at UTC midnight
findings.claim: (1) No script or documented command stops all five processes instantly: restart_bots.sh:4-8 itself warns that `systemctl restart "jsf-paperbot@*"` "matches zero units and exits 0", RECOVERY.md never mentions stopping, and no deploy/stop_all.sh exists -- the operator must reconstruct five unit names under pressure. (2) The daily kill is not sticky: Risk._roll_day (risk.py:100-112) sets killed=False at UTC midnight, so a bot killed by the loss backstop or a confirmed-breakage probe kill resumes trading unattended hours later. (3) daily_loss_limit only blocks new orders and drops the pending queue (run.py:797-807) -- acceptable since positions self-expire in <=15min, but only if (2) is fixed, because 'killed' currently means 'paused until midnight'.
findings.evidence: risk.py:107-109: "self.day = d; self.day_pnl = 0.0; self.killed = False" with the comment at 104-106: "in paper mode, silently ends the measurement run" -- the reset exists FOR paper mode and has no live guard. restart_bots.sh:4-5: "`systemctl restart \"jsf-paperbot@*\"` matches zero units and exits 0." reports/audit_resume_state.md:53-55 acknowledges "probe-kill auto-resumes at UTC midnight with nobody told" as unbuilt.
findings.failure_scenario: The probe confirms a broken edge at 22:00 UTC (venue re-priced the TWAP contract); the bot kills itself; at 00:00 UTC killed clears, all five bots resume full-size trading into the dead edge overnight, and the aggregate $2,000/day dollar backstop is the only remaining brake -- a realistic four-figure overnight loss on an edge already proven broken. Separately: an operator seeing live misbehavior runs the glob command, sees exit 0, and believes the fleet is stopped while it keeps trading.
findings.fix: Ship deploy/stop_all.sh mirroring restart_bots.sh's unit derivation (COINS from config -> systemctl stop, verify is-active=inactive per unit, exit nonzero otherwise). In live mode make kills sticky: a kill file (logs/<coin>/KILLED) checked by inputs_ok that only an operator command removes; _roll_day must not clear a probe-kill (breakage) in live mode, and any midnight auto-resume must sit behind an explicit config flag defaulting to manual re-arm.

findings.title: No alert path: kills and fill-quality divergence visible only in a local jsonl
findings.claim: The right counters exist (n_sent, n_miss with reasons, n_reject, n_partial, run.py:92-99) and land in a health line every 30s (run.py:740-778), but the only consumers are local files and the manually-run src/status.py. There is no webhook, email, push, or systemd OnFailure= hook anywhere, so a live divergence between real fill quality and the paper model's assumptions -- the number the go/no-go rests on -- is discovered whenever the operator next SSHes in, not within a minute. Acknowledged as open in audit_resume_state.md:52-55 but nothing is built.
findings.evidence: run.py:740: "self.log_decision({ \"kind\": \"health\", ..." -- writes to logs/<coin>/decisions.jsonl only. Grep for alert/webhook/notify/OnFailure across *.py/*.sh returns zero code hits. reports/audit_resume_state.md:52-53: "Alerting (ops MAJOR, launch blocker for live): no push/webhook on kill/halt/feed-death".
findings.failure_scenario: Live at scaled size: real fill behavior against a signed taker (the adverse selection findings.md 8.6 admits is unmodelled -- "an ask is pulled precisely when the puller knows something") makes the actual filled/requested ratio a fraction of paper's while the hit rate on what DOES fill collapses; at 100sh/market and ~50 traded markets before the next manual check, hundreds of dollars of avoidable loss accrue that a 1-minute alert would have capped at one or two markets.
findings.fix: Before live: (a) alert_url in config + post_alert() called on risk-state transitions (kill/halt/probe-kill), feed death (rtds_round_stale, consumer_died), reconcile mismatch, and a NEW live-fill-quality monitor -- rolling 30-order window comparing live filled/requested and miss rate against the paper model's shadow prediction for the same orders, alerting when live < 0.5x paper; (b) OnFailure=jsf-alert@%n.service on every unit so a crash-loop pages; (c) status.py --check mode (exit nonzero on any !! condition) on a 1-minute systemd timer posting to the same webhook.

findings.title: Tick-size contradiction in venue_facts.md must be resolved before the order builder
findings.claim: The microstructure section says tick $0.001 (measured from historical Telonex books) while the execution section says the venue reports orderPriceMinTickSize = 0.01 live, and status.py:332 speaks of quotes at "0.995+", which cannot exist on a 0.01 grid. One of these is wrong or the tick is per-market/regime-dependent; a live FAK whose limit price is off-grid is rejected by the venue.
findings.evidence: venue_facts.md:62: "Tick $0.001; min order ~5 shares." vs venue_facts.md:151-152: "`orderMinSize = 5` shares, `orderPriceMinTickSize = 0.01`." src/status.py:332: "quotes 0.995+".
findings.failure_scenario: The Down-side executable price is computed as min(real Down ask, 1 - Up bid); with an Up bid of 0.005 on a 0.001 grid the mirrored limit 0.995 is off the 0.01 grid -- the live order is rejected as invalid price at exactly the late-window moment the strategy cannot retry, converting a modeled fill into a certain miss (each missed winning fill at the record's ~0.93 avg px forgoes ~7c/share).
findings.fix: In the preflight and in discover(), read each market's actual tick from the CLOB markets endpoint and store it on MarketState; the live order builder rounds buy limits DOWN to the grid and validates size >= orderMinSize; then update venue_facts.md line 62 so the two sections agree.

findings.title: Geoblock preflight exists as a tool but nothing runs it automatically
findings.claim: src/check_geoblock.py correctly encodes the three-tier IP policy and venue_facts.md documents that a blocked host reads all feeds perfectly while every order is rejected -- but no deploy script, unit, or bot startup path invokes it. The current droplet placement (Amsterdam, NL = API-unrestricted tier) is a one-time manual fact nothing re-verifies.
findings.evidence: Grep for check_geoblock across *.sh/*.py finds only its own file and a venue_facts.md mention; droplet_setup.sh units (lines 102-136) contain no ExecStartPre or preflight. venue_facts.md:128-130: "the paper bot looks perfectly healthy while being on a host that could never place a live order."
findings.failure_scenario: A droplet migration, IP reassignment, or policy change moves the host's IP into the close-only tier; the live bot's feeds stay green, every FAK is rejected at validation, and the bot forgoes ~100% of expected P&L (~$100-300/day at initial live caps) until a human reads the reject counter -- with no alert path, potentially days.
findings.fix: Add ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/python3 src/check_geoblock.py to the live unit (nonzero exit blocks start), and have the live client treat >=3 consecutive geo-rejection errors as a feed-death alert condition rather than ordinary misses.

result.clean_areas: Checked hard and found correct: (1) .gitignore does cover both .env (line 1) and bot/config.local.json (line 8), and load_cfg()'s local-merge design correctly keeps host-specific values out of the tracked repo -- the only secret leak found came through committed audit transcripts, not through these files. (2) No wallet-grade key material exists anywhere in the working tree or git history: grep for 0x[0-9a-fA-F]{64} and private-key patterns across all commits found nothing outside the transcript files' own discussion text; the only real secret is the Telonex data key reported above. (3) The paper kill switch's internal semantics are coherent: _process_pending drops queued orders when killed/cooloff (run.py:797-807), pending-queue exposure counts toward sizing (run.py:994-999), the opposite-side guard covers both held and queued orders (run.py:979-985), and risk state (day_pnl, kill, cooloff, probe) genuinely survives restarts via _seed_day_pnl + Risk.seed honoring the logged transition -- the restart-persistence fix from the prior audit is complete for paper mode; my kill-switch finding concerns live semantics (stickiness, stop-all, midnight reset), not a regression. (4) The fee model 0.07*p*(1-p) taker-only matches the live feeSchedule quoted in venue_facts.md:145-149 exactly. (5) venue_facts.md's geoblock tier analysis, the 250ms-hold description, the FAK-over-GTC reasoning (a missed GTC resting near expiry is a free option handed to the market), and the Amsterdam-over-Dublin host conclusion are internally consistent and correctly reasoned.
